![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/e1391a86176b1453c05f6ab43f2b5360fac00287e621d8917a142116990688b2.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+3b$, find $\lambda .$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+3b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $3b.$ So, we first draw the vector $3b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/eadc3cc79d5c0f9b58bd8afc6864dca8e5f794cf398921e2ad540b491819562f.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $3b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =3b+a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =1
$$
